language_versions.title: Rapport de la première réunion du Réseau mondial pour l’élimination de l’onchocercose
language_versions.body_text: Rapport de la première réunion du Réseau mondial pour l’élimination de l’onchocercose 24 juin 2024 | Rapport Télécharger (4,2 MB) Vue d’ensemble Plus de 150 partenaires de la lutte contre l'onchocercose, dont des coordinateurs nationaux de l'onchocercose des ministères de la santé des pays d'endémie et anciennement endémiques, des présidents de comités nationaux d'élimination de l'onchocercose, des experts, des chercheurs, des organisations non gouvernementales, la communauté des donateurs et la société civile, se sont réunis les 1er et 2 novembre 2023 à Saly Mbour, Le Sénégal, pour la première réunion du nouveau Réseau mondial de l'onchocercose pour l'élimination (GONE) dont l'objectif est de renforcer la collaboration entre les pays et les partenaires. La réunion a été l'occasion pour les parties prenantes de GONE d'examiner, de discuter et d'approuver les termes de référence du réseau, de mettre en évidence les progrès réalisés par divers pays vers l'élimination de l'onchocercose et d'explorer de nouvelles opportunités de partenariats pour soutenir les initiatives visant à accélérer l'élimination mondiale. de l'onchocercose. À cette fin, les différents intervenants ont souligné l'importance des partenariats public-privé dans la mobilisation de fonds pour couvrir tous les domaines programmatiques afin d'atteindre les objectifs d'élimination. La réunion a également servi de plate-forme permettant aux participants de renforcer la collaboration mondiale et régionale en partageant les connaissances, les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques entre les pays et les partenaires. Des groupes de travail spécifiques ont été mis en place lors de la conférence pour identifier les défis et discuter des solutions pour accélérer l'élimination. La réunion s'est déroulée en séances plénières et en petits groupes. Les séances plénières ont entendu des présentations sur les principales réalisations, lacunes et défis des pays d'endémie et la manière d'atteindre les objectifs de la feuille de route 2030 pour l'élimination de l'onchocercose, ainsi que des mises à jour du Comité d'experts du Mectizan. La séance technique a fourni des mises à jour sur les diagnostics, la surveillance post-vérification, la recherche et le développement, ainsi que des scénarios d'analyse de rentabilisation pour les nouveaux outils et la gestion de l'épilepsie associée à l'onchocercose. Les participants se sont répartis en petits groupes de travail au cours des quatre séances en petits groupes (sur les termes de référence de GONE ; la cartographie, le suivi et l'évaluation de l'accès et de la logistique ; l'entomologie ; et la collaboration transfrontalière) au cours desquelles les participants ont discuté de leurs commentaires et de leur travail préparatoire sur les questions directrices. . À la fin de la première séance en petits groupes, les termes de référence de GONE ont été approuvés par plus de 90 % des participants. La réunion s'est terminée par les déclarations d'un panel de haut niveau composé de représentants de groupes clés et du ministre de la Santé et de l'Action sociale du gouvernement du Sénégal. Plus de 150 partenaires de la lutte contre l'onchocercose, dont des coordinateurs nationaux de l'onchocercose des ministères de la santé des pays d'endémie et anciennement endémiques, des présidents de comités nationaux d'élimination de l'onchocercose, des experts, des chercheurs, des organisations non gouvernementales, la communauté des donateurs et la société civile, se sont réunis les 1er et 2 novembre 2023 à Saly Mbour, Le Sénégal, pour la première réunion du nouveau Réseau mondial de l'onchocercose pour l'élimination (GONE) dont l'objectif est de renforcer la collaboration entre les pays et les partenaires.

La réunion a été l'occasion pour les parties prenantes de GONE d'examiner, de discuter et d'approuver les termes de référence du réseau, de mettre en évidence les progrès réalisés par divers pays vers l'élimination de l'onchocercose et d'explorer de nouvelles opportunités de partenariats pour soutenir les initiatives visant à accélérer l'élimination mondiale. de l'onchocercose. À cette fin, les différents intervenants ont souligné l'importance des partenariats public-privé dans la mobilisation de fonds pour couvrir tous les domaines programmatiques afin d'atteindre les objectifs d'élimination. La réunion a également servi de plate-forme permettant aux participants de renforcer la collaboration mondiale et régionale en partageant les connaissances, les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques entre les pays et les partenaires. Des groupes de travail spécifiques ont été mis en place lors de la conférence pour identifier les défis et discuter des solutions pour accélérer l'élimination.

La réunion s'est déroulée en séances plénières et en petits groupes. Les séances plénières ont entendu des présentations sur les principales réalisations, lacunes et défis des pays d'endémie et la manière d'atteindre les objectifs de la feuille de route 2030 pour l'élimination de l'onchocercose, ainsi que des mises à jour du Comité d'experts du Mectizan. La séance technique a fourni des mises à jour sur les diagnostics, la surveillance post-vérification, la recherche et le développement, ainsi que des scénarios d'analyse de rentabilisation pour les nouveaux outils et la gestion de l'épilepsie associée à l'onchocercose.

Les participants se sont répartis en petits groupes de travail au cours des quatre séances en petits groupes (sur les termes de référence de GONE ; la cartographie, le suivi et l'évaluation de l'accès et de la logistique ; l'entomologie ; et la collaboration transfrontalière) au cours desquelles les participants ont discuté de leurs commentaires et de leur travail préparatoire sur les questions directrices. . À la fin de la première séance en petits groupes, les termes de référence de GONE ont été approuvés par plus de 90 % des participants.

La réunion s'est terminée par les déclarations d'un panel de haut niveau composé de représentants de groupes clés et du ministre de la Santé et de l'Action sociale du gouvernement du Sénégal.

language_versions.body_text: Relatório da primeira reunião da Rede Global para a Eliminação da Oncocercose, Saly Mbour, Senegal, 1–2 de Novembro de 2023 24 June 2024 | Relatório Baixar (3,8 MB) Visão geral Mais de 150 parceiros no domínio da oncocercose, incluindo coordenadores nacionais da oncocercose dos ministérios da saúde dos países endémicos e anteriormente endémicos, presidentes das comissões nacionais de eliminação da oncocercose, peritos, investigadores, organizações não governamentais, a comunidade de doadores e a sociedade civil reuniram-se de 1 a 2 de Novembro de 2023 em Saly Mbour, Senegal, para a primeira reunião da recém-criada Rede Mundial da Oncocercose para a Eliminação (GONE), cujo objectivo é reforçar a colaboração entre países e parceiros. A reunião proporcionou uma oportunidade para as partes interessadas do GONE reverem, discutirem e aprovarem os termos de referência da rede, para destacarem os progressos alcançados por vários países na eliminação da oncocercose e para explorarem novas oportunidades de parcerias para apoiar iniciativas destinadas a acelerar a eliminação global. Para este efeito, os vários oradores enfatizaram a importância das parcerias público-privadas na mobilização de financiamento para cobrir todas as áreas programáticas para alcançar as metas de eliminação. A reunião serviu também de plataforma para os participantes melhorarem a colaboração global e regional através da partilha de conhecimentos, lições aprendidas e melhores práticas entre países e parceiros. Foram criados grupos de trabalho específicos durante a conferência para identificar desafios e discutir soluções para acelerar a eliminação. A reunião foi conduzida em sessões plenárias e de discussão. As sessões plenárias ouviram apresentações sobre as principais conquistas, lacunas e desafios dos países endémicos e o caminho para alcançar as metas do roteiro para 2030 para a eliminação da oncocercose, bem como actualizações do Comité de Peritos de Mectizan. A sessão técnica forneceu actualizações sobre diagnóstico, vigilância pós-verificação, investigação e desenvolvimento e cenários de negócio para novas ferramentas e gestão da epilepsia associada à oncocercose. Os participantes foram divididos em pequenos grupos de trabalho durante as quatro sessões de discussão (sobre os termos de referência do GONE; mapeamento, monitorização e avaliação do acesso e logística; entomologia; e colaboração transfronteiriça) onde os participantes discutiram o seu feedback e o trabalho preparatório sobre as questões orientadoras . No final da primeira sessão de discussão, os termos de referência do GONE foram endossados ​​por mais de 90% dos participantes. A reunião terminou com declarações de um painel de alto nível de representantes dos principais círculos eleitorais e do Ministro da Saúde e Acção Social do Governo do Senegal. Visão geral

Mais de 150 parceiros no domínio da oncocercose, incluindo coordenadores nacionais da oncocercose dos ministérios da saúde dos países endémicos e anteriormente endémicos, presidentes das comissões nacionais de eliminação da oncocercose, peritos, investigadores, organizações não governamentais, a comunidade de doadores e a sociedade civil reuniram-se de 1 a 2 de Novembro de 2023 em Saly Mbour, Senegal, para a primeira reunião da recém-criada Rede Mundial da Oncocercose para a Eliminação (GONE), cujo objectivo é reforçar a colaboração entre países e parceiros.

A reunião proporcionou uma oportunidade para as partes interessadas do GONE reverem, discutirem e aprovarem os termos de referência da rede, para destacarem os progressos alcançados por vários países na eliminação da oncocercose e para explorarem novas oportunidades de parcerias para apoiar iniciativas destinadas a acelerar a eliminação global. Para este efeito, os vários oradores enfatizaram a importância das parcerias público-privadas na mobilização de financiamento para cobrir todas as áreas programáticas para alcançar as metas de eliminação. A reunião serviu também de plataforma para os participantes melhorarem a colaboração global e regional através da partilha de conhecimentos, lições aprendidas e melhores práticas entre países e parceiros. Foram criados grupos de trabalho específicos durante a conferência para identificar desafios e discutir soluções para acelerar a eliminação.

A reunião foi conduzida em sessões plenárias e de discussão. As sessões plenárias ouviram apresentações sobre as principais conquistas, lacunas e desafios dos países endémicos e o caminho para alcançar as metas do roteiro para 2030 para a eliminação da oncocercose, bem como actualizações do Comité de Peritos de Mectizan. A sessão técnica forneceu actualizações sobre diagnóstico, vigilância pós-verificação, investigação e desenvolvimento e cenários de negócio para novas ferramentas e gestão da epilepsia associada à oncocercose.

Os participantes foram divididos em pequenos grupos de trabalho durante as quatro sessões de discussão (sobre os termos de referência do GONE; mapeamento, monitorização e avaliação do acesso e logística; entomologia; e colaboração transfronteiriça) onde os participantes discutiram o seu feedback e o trabalho preparatório sobre as questões orientadoras . No final da primeira sessão de discussão, os termos de referência do GONE foram endossados ​​por mais de 90% dos participantes.

A reunião terminou com declarações de um painel de alto nível de representantes dos principais círculos eleitorais e do Ministro da Saúde e Acção Social do Governo do Senegal.

title: Translating global and regional political commitments towards ending TB into action in the South-East Asia region, Bangkok, Thailand, 23–25 April 2024

content.body_text: Translating global and regional political commitments towards ending TB into action in the South-East Asia region, Bangkok, Thailand, 23–25 April 2024 24 June 2024 | Meeting report Download (2.4 MB) Overview The South-East (SE) Asia Region has shown enormous political commitment towards ending TB, starting in March 2017, when Ministerial Meeting on Ending TB in the SE Asia Region was held in Delhi. Subsequently, high-level meetings were successfully held in 2018 and 2021. In 2023, a high-level ministerial meeting “Sustain, Accelerate and Innovate to End TB in the South-East Asia Region” was held on 16-17 August 2023, at Gandhinagar, Gujarat with an overall objective of reinvigorating the political commitment and preparation for UNHLM on TB in September 2023. This high-level ministerial meeting led to the “Gandhinagar Declaration”. At the UN high-level meeting (UNHLM) in New York on 22 September 2023, the Heads of the States, Delegates, and Representatives from the Member States committed to a “Political Declaration” that sets ambitious targets for service coverage. In alignment with the DG WHO’s flagship initiative, countries committed to achieving by 2027, at least 90 percent of the estimated number of people who develop TB are to be reached with quality assured diagnosis and treatment, which translates to approximately 45 million people between 2023 and 2027 globally; at least 90 percent of people at high risk of developing tuberculosis are provided with preventive treatment, which translates to providing up to approximately 45 million people with TB preventive treatment globally; 100 percent of people with tuberculosis have access to a health and social benefits package, among other targets. The tuberculosis unit of the WHO South-East (SE) Asia Regional office organizes NTP managers and stakeholders’ meetings to discuss the progress and challenges and share best practices for strengthening the national tuberculosis programmes (NTP) of the Member States. In 2024, the title of this meeting was “Translating global and regional political commitments towards ending TB into action in the South-East Asia Region” held in Bangkok, Thailand from 23-25 April 2024. Translating global and regional political commitments towards ending TB into action in the South-East Asia region, Bangkok, Thailand, 23–25 April 2024

24 June 2024
 | Meeting report
Download (2.4 MB)

Overview

The South-East (SE) Asia Region has shown enormous political commitment towards ending TB, starting in March 2017, when Ministerial Meeting on Ending TB in the SE Asia Region was held in Delhi. Subsequently, high-level meetings were successfully held in 2018 and 2021. In 2023, a high-level ministerial meeting “Sustain, Accelerate and Innovate to End TB in the South-East Asia Region” was held on 16-17 August 2023, at Gandhinagar, Gujarat with an overall objective of reinvigorating the political commitment and preparation for UNHLM on TB in September 2023. This high-level ministerial meeting led to the “Gandhinagar Declaration”.

At the UN high-level meeting (UNHLM) in New York on 22 September 2023, the Heads of the States, Delegates, and Representatives from the Member States committed to a “Political Declaration” that sets ambitious targets for service coverage. In alignment with the DG WHO’s flagship initiative, countries committed to achieving by 2027, at least 90 percent of the estimated number of people who develop TB are to be reached with quality assured diagnosis and treatment, which translates to approximately 45 million people between 2023 and 2027 globally; at least 90 percent of people at high risk of developing tuberculosis are provided with preventive treatment, which translates to providing up to approximately 45 million people with TB preventive treatment globally; 100 percent of people with tuberculosis have access to a health and social benefits package, among other targets. 

The tuberculosis unit of the WHO South-East (SE) Asia Regional office organizes NTP managers and stakeholders’ meetings to discuss the progress and challenges and share best practices for strengthening the national tuberculosis programmes (NTP) of the Member States. In 2024, the title of this meeting was “Translating global and regional political commitments towards ending TB into action in the South-East Asia Region” held in Bangkok, Thailand from 23-25 April 2024.

title: Using frozen saltwater packs for short-term transport of vaccines at -25°C to -15°C

content.body_text: Using frozen saltwater packs for short-term transport of vaccines at -25°C to -15°C Interim guidance, June 2024 23 June 2024 | Technical document Download (670.2 kB) Overview Some of the earliest COVID-19 vaccines deployed during the pandemic had a shorter shelf life at +2°C to +8°C. Therefore, transporting these vaccines in a frozen state is the most viable option to maintain their potency throughout the delivery period. This allows the vaccines to be stored in freezers at the lowest distribution points, extending their shelf life at –25°C to –15°C. However, using regular frozen water packs for transport poses challenges, especially for distant facilities, as these packs can only maintain the –25°C to –15°C range for a limited time. To provide countries with a practical interim solution for effectively transporting vaccines at –25°C to –15°C, the World Health Organization (WHO), in collaboration with PATH, developed guidance on using frozen saltwater packs. This minimally validated protocol is designed for certain COVID-19 vaccines or other emergency-use vaccines that require similar temperature conditions during transport. It is not intended for routine use and should only be employed when no other viable transportation methods are available to maintain the –25°C to –15°C temperature range. content.body_html:
Using frozen saltwater packs for short-term transport of vaccines at -25°C to -15°C

Interim guidance, June 2024

23 June 2024
 | Technical document
Download (670.2 kB)

Overview

Some of the earliest COVID-19 vaccines deployed during the pandemic had a shorter shelf life at +2°C to +8°C. Therefore, transporting these vaccines in a frozen state is the most viable option to maintain their potency throughout the delivery period. This allows the vaccines to be stored in freezers at the lowest distribution points, extending their shelf life at –25°C to –15°C. However, using regular frozen water packs for transport poses challenges, especially for distant facilities, as these packs can only maintain the –25°C to –15°C range for a limited time. To provide countries with a practical interim solution for effectively transporting vaccines at –25°C to –15°C, the World Health Organization (WHO), in collaboration with PATH, developed guidance on using frozen saltwater packs. This minimally validated protocol is designed for certain COVID-19 vaccines or other emergency-use vaccines that require similar temperature conditions during transport. It is not intended for routine use and should only be employed when no other viable transportation methods are available to maintain the –25°C to –15°C temperature range.

title: Laboratory biosecurity guidance

content.body_text: Laboratory biosecurity guidance 21 June 2024 | Guidance (normative) Download (1.1 MB) Overview The WHO laboratory biosecurity guidance follows and complements the revision of the Laboratory biosafety manual, fourth edition and provides principles and measures to prevent lapses and incidents throughout the whole value chain of handling high-consequence biological material, technology and information. The document shares global best practice and covers the biosecurity part of the biological risk management lifecycle, starting from collection, transportation, storage and experiment, and in specific context such as every type of biomedical laboratory, research activities, repository and biobank. It also provides key considerations and best practices for institutional, national and international levels, including regulatory oversight. Key elements of the guidance are: Consequence-driven biosecurity risk assessment Emerging technologies and potential threats (Cybersecurity, information security; molecular techniques, artificial intelligence) International and national legislation/regulation two-tier system of the national body and the institutions using a hybrid approach with risk-based elements of list-based high-consequence material Strengthening the role and responsibility of institutional biosafety committees Ultimate situations – war, civil unrest, devastating natural disasters WHO Team Biosecurity & Health Security Protection (BSP), Epidemic and Pandemic Preparedness and Prevention (EPP) Number of pages 110 Copyright

Laboratory biosecurity guidance

21 June 2024
 | Guidance (normative)
Download (1.1 MB)

Overview

The WHO laboratory biosecurity guidance follows and complements the revision of the Laboratory biosafety manual, fourth edition and provides principles and measures to prevent lapses and incidents throughout the whole value chain of handling high-consequence biological material, technology and information. The document shares global best practice and covers the biosecurity part of the biological risk management lifecycle, starting from collection, transportation, storage and experiment, and in specific context such as every type of biomedical laboratory, research activities, repository and biobank. It also provides key considerations and best practices for institutional, national and international levels, including regulatory oversight. Key elements of the guidance are:

  • Consequence-driven biosecurity risk assessment
  • Emerging technologies and potential threats (Cybersecurity, information security; molecular techniques, artificial intelligence)
  • International and national legislation/regulation
    • two-tier system of the national body and the institutions using a hybrid approach with risk-based elements of list-based high-consequence material
  • Strengthening the role and responsibility of institutional biosafety committees
  • Ultimate situations – war, civil unrest, devastating natural disasters

title: Countdown to 2023: WHO 5-year milestone report on global trans fat elimination 2023

content.body_text: Countdown to 2023: WHO 5-year milestone report on global trans fat elimination 2023 21 June 2024 | Publication Download (3.2 MB) Overview This fifth milestone report summarizes the progress from 2018-2023 towards the global elimination of industrially produced trans -fatty acids (TFA), highlighting impacts on public health. With a focus on public health impact, it summarizes progress towards the global target, highlights progress by WHO region, and describes the remaining challenges and policy recommendations to complete and sustain elimination. Immense advances have been made. In 2023 alone, new best-practice policies became effective in seven countries (Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria, North Macedonia, Philippines, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine). At the end of 2023, WHO-recommended policies were in effect in 53 countries, covering 3.7 billion people or 46% of the world’s population, as compared to 6% just 5 years ago. Current best-practice policies could prevent approximately 66% of the total deaths originally estimated to be caused by TFA intake annually — equivalent to almost 183 000 lives saved each year. By the end of 2025, WHO calls for best-practice policies in countries that together account for at least 90% of the total global TFA burden and at least 70% of the total TFA burden within each region. 21 June 2024

Overview

This fifth milestone report summarizes the progress from 2018-2023 towards the global elimination of industrially produced trans-fatty acids (TFA), highlighting impacts on public health. With a focus on public health impact, it summarizes progress towards the global target, highlights progress by WHO region, and describes the remaining challenges and policy recommendations to complete and sustain elimination.

Immense advances have been made. In 2023 alone, new best-practice policies became effective in seven countries (Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria, North Macedonia, Philippines, Republic of Moldova and Ukraine). At the end of 2023, WHO-recommended policies were in effect in 53 countries, covering 3.7 billion people or 46% of the world’s population, as compared to 6% just 5 years ago. Current best-practice policies could prevent approximately 66% of the total deaths originally estimated to be caused by TFA intake annually — equivalent to almost 183 000 lives saved each year.

By the end of 2025, WHO calls for best-practice policies in countries that together account for at least 90% of the total global TFA burden and at least 70% of the total TFA burden within each region.

title: Guidance for monitoring healthy diets globally

content.body_text: Guidance for monitoring healthy diets globally 21 June 2024 | Publication Download (3 MB) Overview Monitoring of dietary intake at national and global levels is becoming increasingly important with the changing food systems and diets. Better measurement and monitoring are needed to support governments in establishing policies and programmes to promote healthy diets and assess the effectiveness of these actions. However, there is lack of consensus on the indicators that best capture the properties of healthy diets. Recognizing the need for consensus and action, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), and the World Health Organization (WHO), have joined forces to chart a way forward via Healthy Diets Monitoring Initiative (HDMI) . This is the first version of the guidance for monitoring healthy diets globally, which provides an overview of healthy diets measurement purposes, types of surveys suitable for the monitoring purpose, appropriate dietary assessment methods, relevant dietary data types and potential healthy diet metrics for national and global monitoring purposes. The guidance will be enhanced in the coming years to reflect the most up to date technical and operational recommendations, after rounds of consultations with countries and experts actively engaged in the implementation of surveys and data collection processes. Overview

Monitoring of dietary intake at national and global levels is becoming increasingly important with the changing food systems and diets. Better measurement and monitoring are needed to support governments in establishing policies and programmes to promote healthy diets and assess the effectiveness of these actions. However, there is lack of consensus on the indicators that best capture the properties of healthy diets. Recognizing the need for consensus and action, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), and the World Health Organization (WHO), have joined forces to chart a way forward via Healthy Diets Monitoring Initiative (HDMI).

This is the first version of the guidance for monitoring healthy diets globally, which provides an overview of healthy diets measurement purposes, types of surveys suitable for the monitoring purpose, appropriate dietary assessment methods, relevant dietary data types and potential healthy diet metrics for national and global monitoring purposes. The guidance will be enhanced in the coming years to reflect the most up to date technical and operational recommendations, after rounds of consultations with countries and experts actively engaged in the implementation of surveys and data collection processes.

language_versions.body_text: إرشادات لرصد النُظُم الغذائية الصحية على الصعيد العالمي 21 حزيران/يونيو 2024 | المنشور تحميل (2 MB) نظرة عامة بات رصد المدخول الغذائي يحظى بأهمية متزايدة على المستويين الوطني والعالمي في ظل التغير المستمر الذي تشهده النظم والأنماط الغذائية. وثمة حاجة إلى تحسين القياس والرصد لدعم الحكومات في وضع السياسات والبرامج الرامية إلى تعزيز النظم الغذائية الصحية وتقييم فعالية هذه الإجراءات. بيد أنه لا يوجد توافق في الآراء بشأن المؤشرات التي تعبّر عن خصائص النظم الغذائية الصحية على النحو الأفضل. وإدراكاً للحاجة إلى توافق الآراء واتخاذ إجراءات عملية، تظافرت جهود منظمة الأغذية والزراعة للأمم المتحدة (الفاو) ومنظمة الأمم المتحدة للطفولة (اليونيسيف) ومنظمة الصحة العالمية من أجل خطّ مسار للمضي قدماً من خلال مبادرة رصد النظم الغذائية الصحية. وهذه أول نسخة من الإرشادات الخاصة برصد النظم الغذائية الصحية على الصعيد العالمي وتقدَّم فيها لمحة عامة عن أغراض قياس النظم الغذائية الصحية، وأنواع الدراسات الاستقصائية الملائمة لغرض الرصد، وأساليب التقييم الغذائي المناسبة، وأنواع البيانات الغذائية ذات الصلة، ومقاييس النظم الغذائية الصحية التي يمكن الاستعانة بها لأغراض الرصد على المستويين الوطني والعالمي. وستحسَّن الإرشادات في السنوات المقبلة لتعكس أحدث التوصيات التقنية والتشغيلية التي تنبثق عن جولات المشاورات مع البلدان والخبراء المشاركين بنشاط في تنفيذ الدراسات الاستقصائية وعمليات جمع البيانات. فريق منظمه الصحة العالمية Healthy Diets Monitoring Initiative (HDMI), Monitoring and Surveillance Nutrition and Food Safety (MNF), Nutrition and Food Safety (NFS) المحررين منظمة الصحة العاملية, منظمة األغذية والزراعة لألمم املتحدة & منظمة األمم املتحدة للطفولة (‎اليونيسيف)‎. عدد الصفحات 44 الأرقام المرجعية ردمك: 9789240095953 حق المؤلف English 中文 Français Русский Español

نظرة عامة

بات رصد المدخول الغذائي يحظى بأهمية متزايدة على المستويين الوطني والعالمي في ظل التغير المستمر الذي تشهده النظم والأنماط الغذائية. وثمة حاجة إلى تحسين القياس والرصد لدعم الحكومات في وضع السياسات والبرامج الرامية إلى تعزيز النظم الغذائية الصحية وتقييم فعالية هذه الإجراءات. بيد أنه لا يوجد توافق في الآراء بشأن المؤشرات التي تعبّر عن خصائص النظم الغذائية الصحية على النحو الأفضل. وإدراكاً للحاجة إلى توافق الآراء واتخاذ إجراءات عملية، تظافرت جهود منظمة الأغذية والزراعة للأمم المتحدة (الفاو) ومنظمة الأمم المتحدة للطفولة (اليونيسيف) ومنظمة الصحة العالمية من أجل خطّ مسار للمضي قدماً من خلال مبادرة رصد النظم الغذائية الصحية.

وهذه أول نسخة من الإرشادات الخاصة برصد النظم الغذائية الصحية على الصعيد العالمي وتقدَّم فيها لمحة عامة عن أغراض قياس النظم الغذائية الصحية، وأنواع الدراسات الاستقصائية الملائمة لغرض الرصد، وأساليب التقييم الغذائي المناسبة، وأنواع البيانات الغذائية ذات الصلة، ومقاييس النظم الغذائية الصحية التي يمكن الاستعانة بها لأغراض الرصد على المستويين الوطني والعالمي. وستحسَّن الإرشادات في السنوات المقبلة لتعكس أحدث التوصيات التقنية والتشغيلية التي تنبثق عن جولات المشاورات مع البلدان والخبراء المشاركين بنشاط في تنفيذ الدراسات الاستقصائية وعمليات جمع البيانات.

全球健康膳食监测指导文件

2024年6月21日
 | 出版

概述

随着粮食体系和饮食的不断变化，在国家和全球层面监测膳食摄入量变得越来越重要。需要加强衡量和监测，以支持各国政府制定政策和规划，从而促进健康饮食，并评估这些行动的有效性。然而，尚未就最能反映健康饮食特性的指标达成共识。联合国粮食及农业组织（粮农组织）、联合国儿童基金会（儿基会）和世界卫生组织（世卫组织）认识到达成共识和采取行动的必要性，并形成了合力，通过健康饮食监测倡议规划了前进方向。

这是全球健康饮食监测指南的第一版，其中概述衡量健康饮食的目的、切合监测目的的调查类型、适当的饮食评估方法、相关饮食数据类型以及用于国家和全球监测目的的潜在健康饮食指标。未来几年，在与积极参与实施调查和数据收集过程的国家和专家进行多轮磋商后，将加强该指南，以反映最新的技术和行动建议。

language_versions.title: Orientations pour le suivi mondial d’une alimentation saine
language_versions.body_text: Orientations pour le suivi mondial d’une alimentation saine 21 juin 2024 | Publication Télécharger (2,4 MB) Vue d’ensemble Le suivi de l’apport alimentaire au niveau national et mondial prend de plus en plus d’importance avec l’évolution des systèmes et des régimes alimentaires. Il faut améliorer la mesure et le suivi pour aider les gouvernements à mettre en place des politiques et des programmes visant à promouvoir une alimentation saine et à en évaluer l’efficacité. Cependant, il n’y a pas de consensus sur les indicateurs qui rendent le mieux compte des propriétés d’une alimentation saine. Sachant qu’il faut trouver un consensus et agir, l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO), le Fonds des Nations Unies pour l’enfance (UNICEF) et l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) ont uni leurs forces pour tracer la voie à suivre dans le cadre de l’Initiative de suivi pour une alimentation saine. Il s’agit de la première version des orientations pour le suivi mondial d’une alimentation saine, qui décrivent succinctement les objectifs de mesure, les types d’enquêtes appropriées pour le suivi, les méthodes appropriées d’évaluation de l’alimentation, les types de données pertinents et les métriques pouvant être utilisées à l’échelle nationale et mondiale. Ces orientations seront affinées dans les années à venir en fonction des dernières recommandations techniques et opérationnelles, après plusieurs consultations avec les pays et les experts qui participent activement aux enquêtes et à la collecte de données. language_versions.title: Руководство по глобальному мониторингу здорового питания
language_versions.body_text: Руководство по глобальному мониторингу здорового питания 21 июня 2024 г. | Публикации Скачать (2,5 MB) Обзор Мониторинг потребления пищевых продуктов на национальном и глобальных уровнях приобретает все большее значение ввиду изменений в продовольственных системах и рационах питания. Совершенствование показателей и повышение эффективности мониторинга необходимы для того, чтобы помочь государственным органам в разработке мер политики и программ по обеспечению здорового питания и оценке эффективности этой деятельности. Однако консенсуса относительно показателей, которые наиболее полно отражали бы характеристики здорового питания, в настоящее время не существует. Признавая необходимость достижения консенсуса и принятия определенных мер, Продовольственная и сельскохозяйственная организация Объединенных Наций (ФАО), Детский фонд Организации Объединенных Наций (ЮНИСЕФ) и Всемирная организация здравоохранения (ВОЗ), совместно разработали программу дальнейших действий, названную «Инициатива по мониторингу здорового питания» (ИМЗП). Данный документ представляет собой первую версию руководства по мониторингу здорового питания на глобальном уровне, в котором содержится обзор целей применения показателей здорового питания, видов обследований, применимых в целях соответствующего мониторинга, надлежащих методов оценки характеристик питания, соответствующих типов данных о потреблении пищевых продуктов и возможных показателей здорового питания для ведения мониторинга на национальном и глобальных уровнях. Руководство будет дорабатываться в ближайшие годы с учетом актуальных технических и операционных рекомендаций, после проведения раундов консультаций со странами и экспертами, активно участвующими в проведении обследований и процедурах сбора данных. Группа ВОЗ Healthy Diets Monitoring Initiative (HDMI), Monitoring and Surveillance Nutrition and Food Safety (MNF), Департамент по вопросам питания и безопасности пищевых продуктов Редакторы Всемирная организация здравоохранения, Продовольственная и сельскохозяйственная организация Объединенных Наций & Детский фонд Организации Объединенных Наций (‎ЮНИСЕФ)‎. Однако консенсуса относительно показателей, которые наиболее полно отражали бы характеристики здорового питания, в настоящее время не существует. Данный документ представляет собой первую версию руководства по мониторингу здорового питания на глобальном уровне, в котором содержится обзор целей применения показателей здорового питания, видов обследований, применимых в целях соответствующего мониторинга, надлежащих методов оценки характеристик питания, соответствующих типов данных о потреблении пищевых продуктов и возможных показателей здорового питания для ведения мониторинга на национальном и глобальных уровнях. Руководство будет дорабатываться в ближайшие годы с учетом актуальных технических и операционных рекомендаций, после проведения раундов консультаций со странами и экспертами, активно участвующими в проведении обследований и процедурах сбора данных.

language_versions.body_text: Orientaciones para el seguimiento mundial de las dietas saludables 21 de junio de 2024 | Publicación Descargar (2,1 MB) Visión de conjunto La evolución de los regímenes y los sistemas alimentarios obliga cada vez más a hacer un seguimiento de la ingesta de la población a escala nacional y mundial. Es necesario mejorar la medición y el seguimiento para ayudar a los gobiernos a formular políticas y programas de fomento de la alimentación saludable y para evaluar la eficacia de estas medidas. Sin embargo, no hay consenso sobre los indicadores que reflejan mejor cuáles son las características de las dietas saludables. Reconociendo la necesidad de llegar a un consenso y de actuar, la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO), el Fondo de las Naciones Unidas para la Infancia (UNICEF) y la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS) han sumado fuerzas para sentar unas bases en esta esfera a través de la Iniciativa para el Seguimiento de las Dietas Saludables. Esta es la primera versión de las orientaciones para el seguimiento de las dietas saludables a nivel mundial y ofrece una visión general de los objetivos de la medición en este ámbito, los tipos de encuestas adecuadas para cumplir el objetivo del seguimiento, los métodos apropiados de evaluación de la alimentación, los tipos de datos pertinentes y los parámetros de medición de las dietas saludables que se pueden emplear a nivel nacional y mundial. En los próximos años, se introducirán mejoras en las orientaciones para reflejar las recomendaciones técnicas y prácticas más avanzadas, tras realizar rondas de consultas con países y expertos que participen activamente en los procesos de realización de encuestas y recopilación de datos. title: Global alcohol action plan 2022-2030

content.body_text: Global alcohol action plan 2022-2030 20 June 2024 | Governing bodies documentation Download (977.4 kB) Overview The global alcohol action plan 2022-2030, endorsed by WHO Member States, aims to reduce the harmful use of alcohol through effective, evidence-based strategies at national, regional, and global levels. Building on the 2010 WHO Global strategy to reduce the harmful use of alcohol, the plan advocates for high-impact policies, multisectoral action, enhanced health and social care system responses, raising awareness of alcohol risks, and mobilizing necessary resources. It sets specific targets for reducing alcohol consumption and improving health outcomes, with a focus on population’s health and integrating alcohol policy within broader public health agendas. The plan outlines six key areas for action: high-impact strategies and interventions, advocacy and awareness, partnership and coordination, technical support and capacity-building, knowledge production and information systems, and resource mobilization. The action plan encourages collaboration among WHO Member States, international partners, and civil society organizations. Additionally, the plan includes proposed measures for economic operators to contribute to achieving its objectives. The action-oriented approach of the plan is designed to foster effective governance, political commitment, and strategic interventions to protect public health and reduce alcohol-related harms globally. Overview

The global alcohol action plan 2022-2030, endorsed by WHO Member States, aims to reduce the harmful use of alcohol through effective, evidence-based strategies at national, regional, and global levels. Building on the 2010 WHO Global strategy to reduce the harmful use of alcohol, the plan advocates for high-impact policies, multisectoral action, enhanced health and social care system responses, raising awareness of alcohol risks, and mobilizing necessary resources. It sets specific targets for reducing alcohol consumption and improving health outcomes, with a focus on population’s health and integrating alcohol policy within broader public health agendas. The plan outlines six key areas for action: high-impact strategies and interventions, advocacy and awareness, partnership and coordination, technical support and capacity-building, knowledge production and information systems, and resource mobilization. The action plan encourages collaboration among WHO Member States, international partners, and civil society organizations.  Additionally, the plan includes proposed measures for economic operators to contribute to achieving its objectives.  The action-oriented approach of the plan is designed to foster effective governance, political commitment, and strategic interventions to protect public health and reduce alcohol-related harms globally.

language_versions.body_text: 2022-2030年全球酒精行动计划 2024年6月20日 | 理事机构文件 下载 (738.3 kB) 概述 《2022-2030年全球酒精行动计划》得到世卫组织所有会员国的认可，其目的是通过在国家、区域和全球各级实施有效的循证战略，减少有害使用酒精。该计划以2010年世卫组织《减少有害使用酒精全球战略》为基础，倡导采取具有高影响力的政策、开展多部门行动、加强卫生和社会照护系统的应对措施、提高对酒精风险的认识以及调动必要的资源。其中为减少酒精消费和改善健康结果制定了具体目标，重点关注人口健康和将酒精政策纳入更广泛的公共卫生议程。该计划概述了六个关键行动领域，即：高影响力战略和干预措施、宣传和认识、伙伴关系和协调、技术支持和能力建设、知识生产和信息系统以及资源调动。该行动计划鼓励世卫组织会员国、国际伙伴和民间社会组织之间开展合作，并还为经济运营者建议了措施以推动实现行动计划的各项目标。这项以行动为导向的计划旨在促进有效治理、政治承诺和战略干预，从而在全球保护公众健康并减少酒精相关危害 世卫组织团队 酒精、毒品和成瘾行为 （ADA） 页数 32 参考编号 书号: 9789240096707 版权 English العربية Français Русский Español

language_versions.title: Plan d’action mondial contre l’alcool 2022–2030
language_versions.body_text: Plan d’action mondial contre l’alcool 2022–2030 20 juin 2024 | Documentation des organes directeurs Télécharger (1,2 MB) Vue d’ensemble Le Plan d’action mondial contre l’alcool 2022-2030, approuvé par les États Membres de l’OMS, vise à réduire l’usage nocif de l’alcool grâce à des stratégies efficaces et fondées sur des données probantes au niveau national, régional et mondial. S’appuyant sur la Stratégie mondiale visant à réduire l’usage nocif de l’alcool approuvée par l’Assemblée mondiale de la Santé en 2010, le plan préconise des politiques à fort impact, une action multisectorielle, l’amélioration des mesures prises par les systèmes de santé et de protection sociale, une sensibilisation aux risques liés à l’alcool et la mobilisation des ressources nécessaires. Il fixe des objectifs précis pour réduire la consommation d’alcool et améliorer les résultats en matière de santé, en mettant l’accent sur la santé de la population et l’intégration des politiques contre l’alcool dans des programmes de santé publique plus larges. Le plan définit six domaines d’action principaux : application d’options et d’interventions à fort impact, sensibilisation, partenariat et coordination, appui technique et renforcement des capacités, production de connaissances et systèmes d’information, et mobilisation des ressources. Il préconise la collaboration entre les États Membres de l’OMS, les partenaires internationaux et les organisations de la société civile. Il comporte en outre des propositions de mesures pour que les acteurs économiques contribuent à la réalisation des objectifs qui y figurent. language_versions.title: Глобальный план действий по борьбе с алкоголем на 2022-2030 годы
language_versions.body_text: Глобальный план действий по борьбе с алкоголем на 2022-2030 годы 20 июня 2024 г. | Документация руководящих органов Скачать (464,8 kB) Обзор Глобальный план действий по борьбе с алкоголем на 2022–2030 гг., одобренный всеми государствами-членами ВОЗ, направлен на сокращение вредного употребления алкоголя за счет эффективных и научно обоснованных национальных, региональных и глобальных стратегий. План действий, разработанный на основе Глобальной стратегии ВОЗ по сокращению вредного употребления алкоголя 2010 г., призывает к принятию высокоэффективных мер политики, многосекторальной деятельности, усилению мер на уровне системы здравоохранения и социального обеспечения, информированию о рисках употребления алкоголя и мобилизации ресурсов. Он содержит целевые показатели снижения потребления алкоголя и улучшения исходов с акцентом на охрану здоровья населения и интеграцию политики в отношении алкоголя в другие программы здравоохранения. В плане шесть ключевых направлений: высокоэффективные стратегии и мероприятия, информирование и повышение осведомленности, партнерства и координация, техническая поддержка и укрепление потенциала, экспертные знания и информационные системы, мобилизация ресурсов. Его цель – стимулировать сотрудничество государств-членов ВОЗ, международных партнеров и организаций гражданского общества. План также содержит предложения о мерах, которые могут принять экономические субъекты для содействия достижению поставленных целей. Ориентированный на конкретные действия подход, лежащий в основе плана действий, призван способствовать эффективному управлению, политической приверженности и стратегическим действиям в интересах охраны здоровья и снижения вреда от употребления алкоголя во всем мире. language_versions.title: Plan de acción mundial sobre el alcohol 2022-2030
language_versions.body_text: Plan de acción mundial sobre el alcohol 2022-2030 20 de junio de 2024 | Documentación de los órganos rectores Descargar (1,1 MB) Visión de conjunto El Plan de acción mundial sobre el alcohol 2022-2030, aprobado por los Estados Miembros de la OMS, tiene como objetivo reducir el uso nocivo del alcohol a través de estrategias efectivas y basadas en evidencias a nivel nacional, regional y mundial. Basándose en la Estrategia mundial de la OMS de 2010 para reducir el uso nocivo del alcohol, el plan aboga por políticas de alto impacto, acción multisectorial, respuestas mejoradas de los sistemas de salud y asistencia social, mayor concienciación sobre los riesgos del alcohol y la movilización de los recursos necesarios. Establece objetivos específicos para reducir el consumo de alcohol y mejorar los resultados en salud, con un enfoque en la salud de la población y en la integración de la política sobre el alcohol dentro de las agendas de salud pública más amplias. El plan describe seis áreas clave de acción: estrategias e intervenciones de alto impacto, defensa y concienciación, asociación y coordinación, apoyo técnico y desarrollo de capacidades, producción de conocimiento y sistemas de información, y movilización de recursos. El plan de acción fomenta la colaboración entre los Estados Miembros de la OMS, socios internacionales y organizaciones de la sociedad civil. Además, el plan incluye medidas propuestas para que los operadores económicos contribuyan a lograr sus objetivos. El enfoque orientado a la acción del plan está diseñado para promover una gobernanza efectiva, el compromiso político y las intervenciones estratégicas para proteger la salud pública y reducir los daños relacionados con el alcohol a nivel mundial. 20 June 2024
 | Publication
Download (1.7 MB)

Overview

This toolkit is a comprehensive set of practical tools and resources designed to support country-level risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) practitioners, decision-makers, and partners to plan and implement readiness and response activities for dengue fever outbreaks. The toolkit contains: information about dengue fever; RCCE considerations for how to approach key issues during dengue fever outbreaks; tools for understanding the context in which dengue fever outbreaks occur; methods for collecting data to inform strategy development and bring evidence into planning and implementation of activities; guidance to support vector control and prevention activities; case studies; and links to existing RCCE tools and training. It is one of a suite of toolkits on RCCE readiness and response to a range of disease and response areas.

language_versions.body_text: مجموعة أدوات الاستعداد والاستجابة في مجال الإبلاغ عن المخاطر وإشراك المجتمع: حمىالضنك 20 حزيران/يونيو 2024 | ادوات تحميل (1.3 MB) نظرة عامة تتمثل مجموعة األدوات هذه في مجموعة شاملة من األدوات ّمة لدعم الممارسين في مجال اإلبالغموالموارد العملية المص ار، والجهاتعن المخاطر والمشاركة المجتمعية، وصناع القر ي، في تخطيط أنشطة االستعدادُطرقالشريكة على المستوى ال واالستجابة لفاشيات حمى الضنك، وتنفيذها. وتحتوي مجموعة األدوات على ما يلي: معلومات عن حمى الضنك؛ ات الخاصة باإلبالغ عن المخاطر والمشاركةواالعتبار اعاتها عند التعامل مع المسائلالتي ينبغي مر المجتمعية الرئيسية في فاشيات حمى الضنك؛ وأدوات لفهم السياق الذي تحدث فيه فاشيات حمى الضنك؛ وطرق جمع البيانات لالسترشاد بها في وضع اتيجيات وتوفير البيّنات لتخطيط األنشطة وتنفيذها؛االستر إ رشادات لدعم أنشطة مكافحة النواقل والوقاية منها؛او اسات الحاالت؛ودر والروابط المؤدية إلى األدوات الحالية لإلبالغ عن المخاطر والمشاركة المجتمعية والتدريب. ُعد مجموعة األدوات هذه واحدة من سلسلة من مجموعاتتو األدوات الخاصة باالستعداد واالستجابة في مجال اإلبالغ عن اض ومجاالتلطيف من األمر المخاطر والمشاركة المجتمعية االستجابة لها. فريق منظمه الصحة العالمية Community Readiness and Resilience (CRR), Country Readiness Strengthening (CRS), مكافحة أمراض المناطق المدارية المهملة (NTD) المحررين منظمة الصحة العالمية عدد الصفحات 55 الأرقام المرجعية ردمك: 978-92-4-010440-2 حق المؤلف English Français Español Português

language_versions.title: Ensemble d’outils concernant la communication sur les risques et la mobilisation communautaire dans le cadre de la préparation opérationnelle et la riposte face à la dengue
language_versions.body_text: Ensemble d’outils concernant la communication sur les risques et la mobilisation communautaire dans le cadre de la préparation opérationnelle et la riposte face à la dengue 20 juin 2024 | Publication Télécharger (2,2 MB) Vue d’ensemble Cet ensemble d’outils constitue une panoplie complète d’outils et d’instruments pratiques conçus pour aider les professionnels, les décideurs et les partenaires impliqués dans la communication sur les risques et la mobilisation communautaire (CRMC) au niveau national à planifier et à mettre en œuvre des activités concernant la préparation opérationnelle et la riposte en cas de flambée épidémique de dengue. Cet ensemble d’outils contient : des informations sur la dengue ; des observations sur la CRMC permettant de mieux appréhender les questions clés au cours des flambées épidémiques de dengue ; des outils pour comprendre le contexte dans lequel se produisent les flambées épidémiques de dengue ; des méthodes de collecte de données permettant de guider l’élaboration de stratégies et d’utiliser des données probantes dans la planification et la mise en œuvre d’activités ; des orientations pour étayer les activités de prévention et de lutte antivectorielle ; des études de cas ; et des liens vers les outils et les formations existants concernant la CRMC. Il fait partie d’une série d’outils concernant la CRMC dans le contexte de la préparation opérationnelle et de la riposte face à différentes maladies et dans différents domaines d’intervention. language_versions.title: Conjunto de herramientas para la comunicación de riesgos y la participación de la comunidad en la disposición operativa y la respuesta frente al dengue
language_versions.body_text: Conjunto de herramientas para la comunicación de riesgos y la participación de la comunidad en la disposición operativa y la respuesta frente al dengue 20 de junio de 2024 | Publicación Descargar (2,2 MB) Visión de conjunto En el presente documento se ofrece un conjunto completo de herramientas y recursos prácticos cuyo objetivo es ayudar a las instancias decisorias, los asociados y los profesionales que se dedican a la comunicación de riesgos y a la participación de la comunidad (CRPC) a escala nacional durante la planificación y la ejecución de actividades de disposición operativa y respuesta frente a los brotes de dengue. El documento contiene: Información sobre el dengue; consideraciones de CRPC para abordar las cuestiones clave durante los brotes de dengue; herramientas para entender el contexto en el que se producen los brotes de dengue; métodos de recopilación de datos para fundamentar la elaboración de estrategias y aportar una base empírica a la planificación y ejecución de actividades; orientaciones para impulsar las actividades de prevención y control de vectores; estudios de casos; enlaces a las herramientas y los materiales de capacitación sobre CRPC. Forma parte de una serie de conjuntos de herramientas de CRPC que pueden usarse en las fases de disposición operativa y respuesta frente a diferentes enfermedades. Overview

The Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework's Partnership Contribution (PC) High-Level Implementation Plan III (HLIP III) outlines the strategy for strengthening global pandemic influenza preparedness from 2024 to 2030. HLIP III takes into consideration the lessons learned from the response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the gains made over time, including from previous HLIPs, and the broader programmatic and policy context in order to address gaps in pandemic influenza preparedness. Implementation of HLIP III will strengthen global, regional, and country-level pandemic influenza preparedness.

Building health system resilience to public health challenges: guidance for implementation in countries

19 June 2024
 | Guidance (normative)
Download (1 MB)

Overview

Health system resilience is not an inevitable byproduct of any investment in health but must be intentionally programmed and developed with necessary input, investment and contextualization. This technical product aims to guide national, subnational, and global health actors to operationalize the concept of health system resilience for advancement of universal health coverage, health security and ultimately better health for all. It supports the translation of relevant conceptual guidance and high-level recommendations into practical actions.

The specific objectives are to:

  • present a concise overview of the concept of health system resilience;
  • provide a roadmap outlining practical and foundational steps for building health system resilience to be adapted to different contexts;
  • share examples of actions and tools, including stakeholder roles, to support country application of the roadmap.

The target audience for this work is the various stakeholders involved in strengthening health systems and public health including management of emergencies (from prevention and preparedness to response and recovery) and other public health challenges in countries. This ranges from the donors, policy-makers and decision-makers at global, national and subnational levels to the implementing institutions and line managers of health system functions and services across the health system building blocks.

content.body_text: Summary report on the WHO workshop on estimation of respiratory syncytial virus (‎RSV)‎ disease burden based on RSV surveillance of Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System, Geneva, Switzerland, 21-23 June 2023 18 June 2024 | Publication Download (1.5 MB) Overview This report summarizes the proceedings from the “WHO workshop on estimation of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease burden based on RSV surveillance of Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System, Geneva, 21–23 June 2023”. title: Report of the third, fourth and fifth meetings of the Technical Advisory Group on Malaria Elimination and Certification: 17 February, 26 May and 27-28 November 2023

content.body_text: Report of the third, fourth and fifth meetings of the Technical Advisory Group on Malaria Elimination and Certification: 17 February, 26 May and 27-28 November 2023 18 June 2024 | Meeting report Download (171.7 kB) Overview The Technical Advisory Group on Malaria Elimination and Certification (TAG-MEC) was established to advise WHO on malaria-free certification, malaria elimination and prevention of re-establishment. This report describes the proceedings and outcomes of three meetings held by the TAG-MEC in 2023, and particularly: the malaria-free certification of Belize and Cabo Verde; the advance draft of the global guidance on prevention of re-establishment and the proposed changes to the first edition of the framework for malaria elimination; the situation of malaria elimination at the global level; the issue of Plasmodium knowlesi . It is intended for the national programme managers, the ongoing development global guidance and the staff from ministries of health and other departments, partners and donors. title: Evaluation of certain veterinary drug residues in food: ninety-eighth report of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives

organization.who_programme: Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives (JECFA)

content.body_text: Evaluation of certain veterinary drug residues in food: ninety-eighth report of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives WHO technical report series; 1055 18 June 2024 | Report Download (1.1 MB) Overview The JECFA98 meeting, which was jointly hosted by FAO and WHO, evaluated three veterinary drugs in Rome 20–29 February 2024. The report represents JECFA evaluation of technical, toxicological, microbiological and epidemiological data, including the occurrence of and dietary exposure to the veterinary drugs Clopidol, Fumagillin dicyclohexylamine, and Imidacloprid. The Committee also finalized a decision tree for evaluating veterinary drugs for which the dossier submitted by the sponsor was incomplete or outdated. It is available in Annex 1 Guidance for the safety evaluation of residues of veterinary drugs with incomplete data package. title: Joint external evaluation of the International Health Regulations (‎2005)‎ core capacities of Samoa - Mission report, 30 October-3 November 2023

content.body_text: Joint external evaluation of the International Health Regulations (‎2005)‎ core capacities of Samoa - Mission report, 30 October-3 November 2023 18 June 2024 | Country report Download (2.4 MB) Overview During the JEE mission, which took place in Apia from 30 October to 3 November 2023, Samoa’s capacities in 19 technical areas were evaluated through a peer-to-peer consultative process that brought together a multisectoral group of national subject matter experts and the multinational, multidisciplinary expert JEE team for discussion, interaction and selected site visits. After a week of collaborative talks this process led to consensus on scores and priority actions across the 19 technical areas, determined to improve implementation of the IHR (2005) and thereby to enhance health security and the resilience of the Samoan health system. While those areas are addressed in the respective sections of this report, the evaluation also generated five wider, overarching recommendations that, if implemented, will consolidate Samoa’s progress and remove bottlenecks that might impede the implementation of the agreed priority actions. These recommendations, outlined below, address cross-cutting challenges affecting Samoa’s capacities across many of the different technical areas that were explored in greater depth in the JEE process. Overview

During the JEE mission, which took place in Apia from 30 October to 3 November 2023, Samoa’s capacities in 19 technical areas were evaluated through a peer-to-peer consultative process that brought together a multisectoral group of national subject matter experts and the multinational, multidisciplinary expert JEE team for discussion, interaction and selected site visits. After a week of collaborative talks this process led to consensus on scores and priority actions across the 19 technical areas, determined to improve implementation of the IHR (2005) and thereby to enhance health security and the resilience of the Samoan health system. 

While those areas are addressed in the respective sections of this report, the evaluation also generated five wider, overarching recommendations that, if implemented, will consolidate Samoa’s progress and remove bottlenecks that might impede the implementation of the agreed priority actions. These recommendations, outlined below, address cross-cutting challenges affecting Samoa’s capacities across many of the different technical areas that were explored in greater depth in the JEE process.

While those areas are addressed in the respective sections of this report, the evaluation also generated five wider, overarching recommendations that, if implemented, will consolidate Samoa’s progress and remove bottlenecks that might impede the implementation of the agreed priority actions. These recommendations, outlined below, address cross-cutting challenges affecting Samoa’s capacities across many of the different technical areas that were explored in greater depth in the JEE process.

content.body_text: Meeting of Leprosy Programme Managers in the South-East Asia Region Kolkata, India, 11–13 April 2023 ﻿ 17 June 2024 | Report Download (3.7 MB) Overview The meeting of leprosy programme managers in the South-East (SE) Asia Region was convened by the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia (WHO-SEARO) from 11 to 13 April 2023 in Kolkata, India. The meeting was attended by 40 participants, including 15 national focal points from nine countries, five experts, partners, donors and WHO staff members, including those from the Global Leprosy Programme (GLP). The objectives of the meeting were to: review the current situation and progress of leprosy elimination in the Member States; discuss the updates on the new guidance and tools from the Global Leprosy Programme; facilitate experience-sharing and catalyse discussions to identify innovative practices, solutions and remaining gaps across countries to enhance leprosy elimination activities; and determine priority actions and support needs for accelerating leprosy elimination in the Region. Overview

The meeting of leprosy programme managers in the South-East (SE) Asia Region was convened by the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia (WHO-SEARO) from 11 to 13 April 2023 in Kolkata, India. The meeting was attended by 40 participants, including 15 national focal points from nine countries, five experts, partners, donors and WHO staff members, including those from the Global Leprosy Programme (GLP).

The objectives of the meeting were to:

  • review the current situation and progress of leprosy elimination in the Member States;
  • discuss the updates on the new guidance and tools from the Global Leprosy Programme;
  • facilitate experience-sharing and catalyse discussions to identify innovative practices, solutions and remaining gaps across countries to enhance leprosy elimination activities; and
  • determine priority actions and support needs for accelerating leprosy elimination in the Region.

content.body_text: Asia Pacific Health Security Action Framework 14 June 2024 | Publication Download (5.3 MB) Overview Public health emergencies, including pandemics, highlight the need for health systems and services that are prepared, resilient and ready to respond to health security threats. Endorsed by Member States in 2023, the Asia Pacific Health Security Action Framework (‎APHSAF)‎ is designed to engage multisectoral actors in health security, and to reflect the complex nature of current and future public health emergencies. The Framework presents six interconnected, multisectoral domains of work that together form a comprehensive, multi-hazard health security system — emphasizing the One Health approach. The Framework also supports progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals and universal health coverage while meeting the responsibilities and obligations of the International Health Regulations (‎2005)‎. content.body_text: Dynamic preparedness metric: methodology report 14 June 2024 | Publication Download (4.1 MB) Overview The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed the Dynamic Preparedness Metric (DPM) to support country preparedness for health emergencies. The DPM can inform countries of their preparedness status and support prioritization and implementation of specific actions to improve capacities. By providing a dynamic, evidence-based, risk-based metric the DPM signals a shift in the paradigm of measuring and acting for preparedness. The DPM varies from the multiple indices that currently exist to measure a country’s health emergency preparedness status which are cross-sectional, do not reflect current and changing risks, particularly as demonstrated by the COVID-19 pandemic, and are not linked to implementable actions. The DPM addresses the gap in linking risk to action for health emergency preparedness. title: Fiscal policies to promote healthy diets: WHO guideline

content.body_text: Fiscal policies to promote healthy diets: WHO guideline 14 June 2024 | Guideline Download (1.7 MB) Overview In current food environments, energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods are readily available, heavily marketed and relatively cheap. Consumers are challenged to make healthy and affordable food-related decisions that are consistent with a healthy diet. Affordability of food is a key determinant of the food environment and changes in price influence consumer demand for many foods and beverages. Fiscal measures, including both taxation and subsidies have long been recognized as a viable policy option to promote healthy diets. Despite some progress in implementing fiscal measures, governments continue to face challenges in their attempts to develop such measures. This WHO guideline provides Member States with recommendations and implementation considerations on fiscal policies to promote healthy diets, including on food and beverage taxation, and on food subsidies that have the primary intention to change consumer behaviour by lowering prices of targeted products at retail level. Guidelines on other policies to improve the food environment are currently under development. Fiscal measures, including both taxation and subsidies have long been recognized as a viable policy option to promote healthy diets. Despite some progress in implementing fiscal measures, governments continue to face challenges in their attempts to develop such measures.

This WHO guideline provides Member States with recommendations and implementation considerations on fiscal policies to promote healthy diets, including on food and beverage taxation, and on food subsidies that have the primary intention to change consumer behaviour by lowering prices of targeted products at retail level.

Guidelines on other policies to improve the food environment are currently under development.

Overview

The World Health Organization’s (WHO) “2023 Antibacterial agents in clinical and preclinical development: an overview and analysis” report evaluates the pipeline of antibacterial candidates in different stages of development.  

This report presents an analysis of antibacterial agents in preclinical (fourth annual review) and clinical (sixth annual review) development. The analysis covers traditional (direct-acting small molecules) and non-traditional antibacterial agents in development worldwide. It evaluates to what extent the present pipeline addresses infections caused by priority pathogens according to the updated 2024 WHO bacterial priority pathogens list. The report also provides an assessment of the traditional agents with respect to whether they meet a set of predefined criteria for innovation, namely absence of known cross-resistance, new target, mode of action and/or class. This report is part of the WHO’s efforts to prioritize and coordinate global research and development (R&D) efforts to address the ongoing void in antibacterial drug development.

Colombo, Sri Lanka, 25 – 27 July 2023 Colombo, Sri Lanka, 25 – 27 July 2023 14 June 2024 | Meeting report Download (5.1 MB) Overview Since 2017, the collaborative efforts of the Food and Agricultural Organization of United Nations, World Health Organization and the World Organisation for Animal Health have led to the development and roll-out of the Joint Risk Assessment (JRA) Operational Tool (OT), a practical instrument linked to the Tripartite Zoonoses Guide. Since 2017, the collaborative efforts of the Food and Agricultural Organization of United Nations, World Health Organization and the World Organisation for Animal Health have led to the development and roll-out of the Joint Risk Assessment (JRA) Operational Tool (OT), a practical instrument linked to the Tripartite Zoonoses Guide. This meeting was held to strengthen JRA using a One Health approach in the WHO South-East Asia Region. title: Developing a strategic plan for the elimination of visceral leishmaniasis in eastern Africa. Report of a stakeholder meeting, Nairobi, Kenya, 24–27 January 2023

content.body_text: Developing a strategic plan for the elimination of visceral leishmaniasis in eastern Africa. Report of a stakeholder meeting, Nairobi, Kenya, 24–27 January 2023 11 June 2024 | Guidance (normative) Download (728.3 kB) Overview The World Health Organization (WHO), in collaboration with the END Fund and the Drugs for Neglected Diseases Initiative (DNDi) and with the participation of the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR), convened a meeting of national programme managers, donors, partners and stakeholders in Nairobi, Kenya on 24–27 January 2023 to develop a strategic framework for the elimination of visceral leishmaniasis (VL) in eastern Africa. The four-day meeting was attended by more than 90 participants including representatives from the health ministries of Chad, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda. The objectives of the meeting were: (i) to review the current epidemiological situation of VL in the world and in countries of the eastern Africa subregion; (ii) to finalize a high-level strategic framework for the elimination of VL as a public health problem 2023–2030, with subregional and country-level targets; (iii) to develop a framework on long-term financing mechanisms including sustained procurement and medical supplies (first-line treatment and diagnostic tests); and (iv) to develop a call for action (the Nairobi declaration) by the Member States and stakeholders. The meeting was conducted in technical sessions, a high-level round table, group work, plenaries and extensive discussions leading to conclusions and recommendations agreed by consensus for action. Conclusions and recommendations VL is a severe clinical disease in the eastern Africa subregion. The disease is outbreak-prone and fatal. In the past four decades, more than 100 000 case fatalities attributable to VL have occurred in this subregion, demonstrating the devastating impact of this chronic illness. Eight countries (Chad, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, South Sudan, Somalia, Sudan, and Uganda) share more than 60% of the global burden of the disease. More than 50% of new cases occur in children and young adults. The disease is associated with malnutrition, poverty, population displacement, migration, climate change and lack of economic resources. Elimination of VL is linked with and will contribute to achieving several of the Sustainable Development Goals, namely Goal 1 (No poverty), Goal 2 (Zero hunger), Goal 3 (Good health and well-being), Goal 5 (Gender equality), Goal 8 (Decent work and economic growth), Goal 10 (Reduced inequalities) and Goal 13 (Climate action). Successes and lessons learnt were presented from the VL elimination initiative of the WHO South-East Asia Region and from the kala-azar elimination programme in India. Since the launch of the initiative in 2005, the incidence of new cases has fallen by 97%, due to, among other factors, political commitment and the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding among endemic countries of the region. The participants recommended unanimously to launch an initiative to eliminate VL as a public health problem in the eastern Africa subregion to reduce neglect, inequalities, and social and economic impacts. A major outcome of the high-level round table discussions was an agreement to sign a Memorandum of Understanding among the eight countries to reflect political commitment. National programme managers and stakeholders issued the Nairobi Declaration to highlight the key focus areas on the path of elimination. WHO was requested to constitute an eastern African (WHO African and Eastern Mediterranean regions) technical advisory group to review progress and provide strategic directions for implementing the strategic framework in endemic countries. The four-day meeting was attended by more than 90 participants including representatives from the health ministries of Chad, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda. The objectives of the meeting were: (i) to review the current epidemiological situation of VL in the world and in countries of the eastern Africa subregion; (ii) to finalize a high-level strategic framework for the elimination of VL as a public health problem 2023–2030, with subregional and country-level targets; (iii) to develop a framework on long-term financing mechanisms including sustained procurement and medical supplies (first-line treatment and diagnostic tests); and (iv) to develop a call for action (the Nairobi declaration) by the Member States and stakeholders. The meeting was conducted in technical sessions, a high-level round table, group work, plenaries and extensive discussions leading to conclusions and recommendations agreed by consensus for action. Conclusions and recommendations VL is a severe clinical disease in the eastern Africa subregion. The disease is outbreak-prone and fatal. In the past four decades, more than 100 000 case fatalities attributable to VL have occurred in this subregion, demonstrating the devastating impact of this chronic illness. Eight countries (Chad, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, South Sudan, Somalia, Sudan, and Uganda) share more than 60% of the global burden of the disease. More than 50% of new cases occur in children and young adults. The disease is associated with malnutrition, poverty, population displacement, migration, climate change and lack of economic resources. Elimination of VL is linked with and will contribute to achieving several of the Sustainable Development Goals, namely Goal 1 (No poverty), Goal 2 (Zero hunger), Goal 3 (Good health and well-being), Goal 5 (Gender equality), Goal 8 (Decent work and economic growth), Goal 10 (Reduced inequalities) and Goal 13 (Climate action). Successes and lessons learnt were presented from the VL elimination initiative of the WHO South-East Asia Region and from the kala-azar elimination programme in India. Since the launch of the initiative in 2005, the incidence of new cases has fallen by 97%, due to, among other factors, political commitment and the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding among endemic countries of the region. The participants recommended unanimously to launch an initiative to eliminate VL as a public health problem in the eastern Africa subregion to reduce neglect, inequalities, and social and economic impacts. A major outcome of the high-level round table discussions was an agreement to sign a Memorandum of Understanding among the eight countries to reflect political commitment. National programme managers and stakeholders issued the Nairobi Declaration to highlight the key focus areas on the path of elimination. WHO was requested to constitute an eastern African (WHO African and Eastern Mediterranean regions) technical advisory group to review progress and provide strategic directions for implementing the strategic framework in endemic countries.

This framework addresses the last of the three steps. title: The adolescent health indicators recommended by the Global Action for Measurement of Adolescent health

content.body_text: The adolescent health indicators recommended by the Global Action for Measurement of Adolescent health Guidance for monitoring adolescent health at country, regional and global levels 10 June 2024 | Guidance (normative) Download (4.4 MB) Overview About 1.3 billion of the world’s population are adolescents, defined as those aged 10-19 years. Adolescents bear long periods of exposure to, and consequences of health risks yet are often least able to influence their environment and make decisions for their own well-being. Historically, the world has lacked comprehensive indicators for adolescent health, which has hindered the effective development of age-specific policies and interventions and tracking of progress towards health targets. This document presents a list of 47 indicators recommended by the Global Action for Measurement of Adolescent health (GAMA), established in 2018 by WHO in collaboration with UNAIDS, UNESCO, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, the World Bank Group, and the World Food Programme. The 47 adolescent health indicators are the result of a structured, participatory 5-year selection process. They are applicable to all adolescent population subgroups and span six domains: (1) programmes, policies and laws, (2) systems performance and interventions, (3) social, cultural, economic, educational, and environmental health determinants, (4) health behaviours and risks, (5) subjective well-being and (6) health outcomes and conditions. Most countries already have data for many of these indicators available. Bringing this information together will help benchmark progress, identify priorities for action, and allocate resources efficiently. By prioritizing adolescent health, young individuals are empowered to reach their full potential, and contribute to building healthier and sustainable communities and societies. The adolescent health indicators recommended by the Global Action for Measurement of Adolescent health

Guidance for monitoring adolescent health at country, regional and global levels

10 June 2024
 | Guidance (normative)
Download (4.4 MB)

Overview

About 1.3 billion of the world’s population are adolescents, defined as those aged 10-19 years. Adolescents bear long periods of exposure to, and consequences of health risks yet are often least able to influence their environment and make decisions for their own well-being.

Historically, the world has lacked comprehensive indicators for adolescent health, which has hindered the effective development of age-specific policies and interventions and tracking of progress towards health targets.

This document presents a list of 47 indicators recommended by the Global Action for Measurement of Adolescent health (GAMA), established in 2018 by WHO in collaboration with UNAIDS, UNESCO, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, the World Bank Group, and the World Food Programme.

The 47 adolescent health indicators are the result of a structured, participatory 5-year selection process. They are applicable to all adolescent population subgroups and span six domains: (1) programmes, policies and laws, (2) systems performance and interventions, (3) social, cultural, economic, educational, and environmental health determinants, (4) health behaviours and risks, (5) subjective well-being and (6) health outcomes and conditions.

Most countries already have data for many of these indicators available. Bringing this information together will help benchmark progress, identify priorities for action, and allocate resources efficiently. By prioritizing adolescent health, young individuals are empowered to reach their full potential, and contribute to building healthier and sustainable communities and societies.

language_versions.body_html:
衡量青少年健康全球行动建议的 青少年健康指标

在国家、区域和全球各级监测 青少年健康指南

2024年6月10日
 | 指导
下载 (4.4 MB)

概述

世界上约有13亿人口是青少年，其定义为年龄在10至19岁之间的人群。青少年面临着长期的健康风险暴露及其后果，但往往最难以改变所处的环境，为自身健康福祉做出决策。

长期以来，全球缺乏全面的青少年健康指标，这阻碍了制定针对不同年龄段的政策和干预措施的有效性，也影响了对健康目标进展的追踪。本文介绍了全球青少年健康测量行动（GAMA）推荐的47项指标。GAMA由世界卫生组织（WHO）于2018年与联合国艾滋病规划署（UNAIDS）、联合国教科文组织（UNESCO）、联合国人口基金（UNFPA）、联合国儿童基金会（UNICEF）、联合国妇女署（UN Women）、世界银行集团和世界粮食计划署共同建立。

这47项青少年健康指标是通过一个结构化的、为期五年的参与式过程筛选得出的，适用于所有青少年群体，涵盖六个领域：(1) 项目、政策和法律，(2) 系统绩效和干预措施，(3) 社会、文化、经济、教育和环境健康决定因素，(4) 健康行为和风险，(5) 主观幸福感，以及 (6) 健康结果和状况。

大多数国家已具备其中许多指标的数据。将这些信息整合起来，有助于衡量进展、确定行动优先事项，并高效分配资源。优先关注青少年健康，能够赋予年轻人实现其全部潜力的能力，并推动建设更加健康和可持续的社区和社会。
